claims.text: Mn in equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni introduces magnetic frustration.
Magnetic frustration raises the energy barrier for deformation-induced FCC-to-HCP transformation.
The increased transformation barrier reduces the HCP phase fraction formed during deformation.
Suppression of HCP formation alters strain-hardening behavior.
The compared alloys can be prepared as single-phase FCC materials using identical thermomechanical treatments.
The relevant structural mediator is the emergence or suppression of a deformation-induced FCC-to-HCP transformation.
Mn-lean quaternary or ternary alloys undergo FCC-to-HCP transformation more readily than the quinary alloy.
Relative to equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni, Mn-lean alloys will form a higher HCP phase fraction at high strain.
The higher HCP phase fraction in Mn-lean alloys will correlate with a change in strain-hardening behavior.
Increasing magnetic-field intensity will further suppress FCC-to-HCP transformation in the quinary alloy.
The proposed mechanism is applicable from room temperature to moderately elevated temperatures under otherwise identical deformation conditions.
Comparable HCP fractions and strain-hardening behavior in the quinary and Mn-lean alloys would falsify the hypothesis.
A lack of systematic transformation response to magnetic-field intensity would falsify the proposed magnetic mechanism.
